description: Two oscillators driving an eight-bit shift register: each clock combines the data state with the register's oldest bit by exclusive or and pushes it in at the front

params.text: Sets the clock oscillator's frequency, twenty octaves from about 0.03Hz to about 32768Hz
Sets the data oscillator's frequency, twenty octaves from about 0.03Hz to about 32768Hz
Scales the clock oscillator's unmarked modulation input, 0 to 1, before it is added to the clock frequency
Scales the data oscillator's marked modulation input, -1 to +1, before it is added to the data frequency
Scales the clock oscillator's marked modulation input, -1 to +1, before it is added to the clock frequency
Scales the data oscillator's unmarked modulation input, 0 to 1, before it is added to the data frequency

inputs.text: Modulates the clock oscillator's frequency through its attenuator, a volt an octave
Modulates the data oscillator's frequency through its attenuverter, a volt an octave
Modulates the clock oscillator's frequency through its attenuverter, a volt an octave
Modulates the data oscillator's frequency through its attenuator, a volt an octave
Sets the clock oscillator's pitch with no attenuation, a volt an octave, added to everything else
The data state read on each clock pulse; above 1.8V counts as high, and with nothing patched it reads the data oscillator's square wave
Clocks the shift register on each rise past 1.8V; with nothing patched it is clocked by the clock oscillator's square wave
Sets the data oscillator's pitch with no attenuation, a volt an octave, added to everything else

outputs.text: The clock oscillator's triangle wave, -5V to +5V
The clock oscillator's square wave, -5V or +5V, which also clocks the shift register when its input is empty
The data oscillator's triangle wave, -5V to +5V
The data oscillator's square wave, -5V or +5V, which also feeds the register's data input when that input is empty
The last three bits of the register read as a binary number, 0V to 4.38V in eight steps
The exclusive or of the data state and the register's oldest bit, 0V or 5V, which usually runs at an eighth of the clock
The stepped output through a first-order lowpass at 20Hz, 0V to 4.38V

notes: nothing has to be patched for the register to run: with the clock and data inputs empty it is driven by the two oscillators' own square waves
feeding a steady 0V into the data input makes the register cycle through a fixed eight-step pattern, because exclusive or with zero passes the bit through unchanged
patching an oscillator's own square or triangle output back into one of its modulation inputs changes the shape of the wave as well as its pitch
